quotes.text: We plan to stop Sources API support for card payments, and to stop support for [Cards](https://docs.stripe.com/api/cards.md).
To migrate your integration, update your server and front end to use the [Payment Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents.md).
Don’t rely solely on the user returning to the `return_url`
By contrast, a `PaymentMethod` is stateless, relying on the PaymentIntent object to represent payment state.

old_evidence.text: If the customer doesn’t complete the payment within 48 hours, then the PaymentIntent transitions to `requires_payment_method` and you can retry the confirmation.
To preserve your existing customers’ saved payment methods, you must convert those sources to payment methods using a data migration tool in the Stripe Dashboard.

It replaces April's local Sources migration announcement and then-no-card-shutoff statement on this route, without establishing effective dates or reversing the separate local-method notice (old raw lines 8–12; new raw lines 9–13).

The card migration mandate and companion changes are distinct from omissions.

answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/transitioning is a full, card-oriented overview. It plans to stop Sources API card support and legacy Cards support, requires existing Sources card integrations to migrate to Payment Intents, and links a separate detailed migration guide (new raw lines 9-25). The merchant creates a Checkout Session or PaymentIntent on the server. Payment Element and custom-form paths use the client secret and Stripe.js. A PaymentMethod represents the instrument while the PaymentIntent owns payment state. The guide describes succeeded, requires_payment_method and requires_action, possibly for 3DS, and requires server retrieval or server webhook verification rather than browser return (new raw lines 27-49 and 76-85). April emphasized local Sources and said no planned card shutdown, gave a 48-hour local authorization example and discussed reusable local Sources and compatible saved cards (old raw lines 8-12, 38-46 and 100-132). source-stripe-legacy-apis.md already flags key differences but needs the direct November raw route and event boundaries.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/transitioning, the substantive change is the planned Sources card and Cards cutoff and mandatory card-path migration after April's local-method focus and no planned card shutdown (old raw lines 8-12; new raw lines 9-13). The same-day Older APIs overview still deprecates card Sources without a then-planned cutoff. Preserve that conflict, no effective cutoff date, the April 48-hour example and local reusable-data conversion, and the distinct November detailed card compatibility limits in source-stripe-legacy-apis.md (old raw lines 38-46 and 100-132; new raw lines 39-49 and 76-95). Retain Checkout, Payment Element and custom form choices, server confirmation evidence and the separate Checkout and Intent event routes (old raw lines 26-32 and 60-71; new raw lines 27-33 and 63-74). Table markup, typographic changes and the detailed migration link are presentation/navigation. Keep reciprocal Payment Methods and Payment Intents routes and both dated raws, alongside the separate Charges, Sources and detailed card migration authority.
